title: Who would you cast in which role, if they did this? #broadway #musica...
transcript: hey with all the gender swapped casting on Broadway right now can we acknowledge how ridiculous it is that Hamilton has never done this for any of its principal roles? I mean we got Megan Thee Stallion in Moulin Rouge we're getting Sherri Shepherd as the Genie in Aladdin we got Lilias white as Hermes in Hadestown We just found out about Stella Cole as the Jazz Singer in maybe happy ending and there have been tons of examples of this going back decades not just revivals that reimagine a character as a different gender but literally a replacement within the same production and Hamilton just feels like such an obvious candidate for gender diverse casting partly just from a functional standpoint of like because it's already cast racially diverse our minds are already primed to suspend our disbelief however we need to but even thematically like in the same way that the racially diverse casting is a deliberate device to comment on sort of reclaiming the narrative of American history casting women in some of these roles could follow in that same vein and add an additional dimension to that Lin-Manuel Miranda even said in 2015 that he would be totally down for this so why has it never happened? *maybe* there's a case to be made that just because there's so much ensemble singing it would make transposition a little harder? but still it feels like that's a problem we could work around especially because so much of the show is rapping you mightnot even have to transpose all of it plus not to get too cynical about it but I'm sure it would make some headlines get people talking about the show and you know with the way they're bringing back original cast members clearly that's on their minds. and if they're lacking for ideas feel free to put some in the comments!
classificationReason: Creator discusses the absence of gender-swapped casting in Hamilton and why it should happen, citing other shows as examples. No first-hand opinion on attending a specific production; this is commentary/discussion about casting.
